description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related quantities (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.81 to 0.99 with tick labels shown at irregular intervals including 0.81, 0.82, 0.84, 0.85, and then roughly every 0.01 up to 0.99. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, and shows regularly spaced tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 1.00 at confidence 0.81, stays in the high range around ~0.90–0.97 across most x-values (e.g., about 0.91 at 0.82, about 0.97 at 0.90, about 0.86 at 0.95), and ends near ~0.98 at 0.99. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars; it begins around ~0.46 at 0.81, generally declines with fluctuations (e.g., ~0.39 at 0.82, ~0.14 at 0.86, ~0.37 at 0.88, ~0.24–0.26 around 0.90–0.91, ~0.30 at 0.93), and finishes near ~0.04 at 0.99. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and error bars; it starts around ~0.54 at 0.81, varies between roughly ~0.52 and ~0.76 through mid-range confidences (e.g., ~0.52 at 0.82, ~0.63 at 0.84, ~0.75 at 0.89, ~0.65 at 0.91, ~0.76 at 0.96), then rises toward the end to about ~0.82 at 0.98 and about ~0.94 at 0.99.
